task.title: Show and manage task dependencies in the web UI
task.description:
Make task dependencies visible and safely editable for human users of the local web app. On board cards, show dependency progress and clearly identify Ready tasks that are not eligible because prerequisites remain unfinished. On the existing task detail route, add a Dependencies section that resolves each prerequisite to its task title, status, priority, and link while retaining the full task ID. Let users add an active task as a prerequisite through an accessible searchable/select control and remove any existing prerequisite.

Use dedicated dependency add/remove HTTP mutations backed by the core DependMutation and FreeMutation operations; do not replace the complete dependency collection through the general task PATCH. Await the Git-durable mutation response, surface warnings and validation failures, then refresh client task state before rerendering. Exclude the current task, existing dependencies, and tombstoned tasks from the add picker. Existing missing or tombstoned dependency IDs must remain visible with an unavailable/deleted state and must still be removable. Preserve the local loopback-only server and versioned JSON/error contracts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Board cards with dependencies show completed versus total prerequisites and distinguish a Ready-but-ineligible task; cards without dependencies remain unchanged.
- The detail route lists and links resolvable dependencies and displays an explicit fallback for missing or tombstoned dependencies.
- A user can add and remove dependencies from an existing task without leaving the detail route; dependency editing during task creation and reverse depended-on-by views are out of scope.
- Self-dependencies, cycles, missing candidates, stale task data, and server failures surface actionable errors without discarding unsaved task-form fields.
- Each successful add/remove uses the same append-only Git-backed set operation and warnings as workbook depend/free; removal remains idempotent.
- Handler and executable client tests cover endpoint methods/documents, cycle and missing-task errors, candidate filtering, board eligibility summaries, detail rendering, durable add/remove refreshes, and failure recovery. Run focused web/core tests plus the full Go tests, go vet, production build, and git diff --check.
